text: . India began Day 12 of the Asian Games 2026 with hopes of adding more medals to their tally today, with several key events lined up across disciplines.India bagged their first sailing medal at the 2026 Asian Games as Manu Francis and Prince Kurisinkal Noble claim silver in the men’s skiff event, finishing just behind China.Across nine races over recent days, Francis and Noble demonstrated impressive consistency, collecting 23 total points and claiming a victory in one of the races to seal the silver spot.In squash, India settled for a bronze medal after losing 1-2 to Hong Kong in the women’s team semifinal. Meanwhile, in sepaktakraw, India assured itself of at least a bronze medal after defeating Vietnam 2-nil in the men’s quadrant event to advance to the semifinals.In the men’s hockey semi-final, India will take on arch-rivals Pakistan in a highly anticipated clash. The Indian team will be aiming for a win to secure its place in the final. Meanwhile, the Indian women’s hockey team has already secured its place in the gold-medal match against China.In Cricket, defending champions India return to action as Shreyas Iyer and company will face Sri Lanka in the men’s semi-final. India will look to secure a victory and move one step closer to defending their Asian Games title.Elsewhere, Indian athletes will be competing across a wide range of sports, including shooting, judo, track cycling, golf, canoe slalom, taekwondo, tennis, sepak takraw, rugby sevens and sport climbing. India’s overall tally has reached 62, including 10 gold, 22 silver and 30 bronze.

. India’s industrial output, as measured by the Index of Industrial Production (IIP), grew by 8% year-on-year in August this year. The latest data indicate that industrial activity continued to expand at a healthy pace, with the upward revision in July’s IIP growth to 7.4% from the earlier estimate of 6.7%.According to government data released today, electricity and gas supply recorded strong growth of 12.3% in August, while manufacturing, which carries the heaviest weight in the index, expanded by 9%. Water supply, sewerage and waste management also registered healthy growth of 6.3%. However, the mining sector remained a laggard, contracting by 5.6% during the period under review.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices witnessed a sharp decline and were trading around 1.3% lower during the afternoon session. The Sensex tumbled 956 points to 72,939, while the Nifty shed 306 points to 22,835 when reports last came in.In the broader market at the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index fell 1.4%, while the Smallcap 100 index slid 1.6% a short while ago. On the sectoral front, all sectors were trading in the red, as a broad-based sell-off was seen across the board.

. The Government has advised Indian nationals against voluntarily giving up their Indian citizenship to join the Russian armed forces. In a statement, the Ministry of External Affairs advised Indian nationals travelling to Russia to exercise caution when pursuing job opportunities there.The Ministry cautioned that voluntarily seeking offers to join the Russian armed forces is dangerous and strongly discouraged by the government. The Ministry said foreign nationals are being recruited into the Russian armed forces by non-public entities, including voluntary organisations. It advised Indian nationals to exercise due diligence before accepting job offers from such agents and organisations, particularly those that are not registered with the Ministry of External Affairs

. President Droupadi Murmu today praised Captain Smit Machchhar and said that the nation is proud of him. In a social media post, President Murmu said that his heroic courage and incredible presence of mind have touched everyone.The President highlighted that even after being seriously injured in a moment of grave peril, he remained determined to protect the lives of others. She noted that his bravery and quick response helped prevent a major tragedy and saved many precious lives. President Murmu also prayed for his speedy recovery and good health and saluted Captain Machchhar’s indomitable spirit.Vice-President  C. P. Radhakrishnan also said that Captain Smit Machchhar’s exceptional courage and presence of mind in the face of grave danger command the highest respect and admiration.In a social media post, Mr Radhakrishnan noted that despite being seriously injured, his determination and decisive action mid-air helped avert a catastrophic tragedy and protect the lives of those on board. The Vice President also prayed for Captain Machchhar’s speedy and complete recovery. He said that the nation is proud of this extraordinary hero.External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar has lauded Captain Smit Machchhar’s extraordinary courage and remarkable presence of mind during the Flydubai flight incident that occurred yesterday. In a social media post, Dr Jaishankar said that Mr Machchhar has saved hundreds of lives and averted a major tragedy even in the face of grave danger.Minister of State for External Affairs,  Kirti Vardhan Singh, said that Captain Smit Machchhar proved that true heroes rise in the darkest hours.In a social media post, Mr Singh commended the Indian pilot for putting the safety of others first despite severe injuries and said that he prevented a massive catastrophe with his selfless bravery. He added that the entire country holds him in the highest regard and prays for his complete and swift recovery.Meanwhile, Ministry of External Affairs Spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal also praised the bravery of Captain Smit Machchhar, who, in spite of being gravely injured, showed courage that saved the lives of many.The Spokesperson informed that Captain Machchhar is receiving medical attention and is safe. He said that the nation proudly stands with him and his family. He also prayed for his speedy recovery.Saudi authorities have arrested an Omani co-pilot after he stabbed the captain and attempted to crash a Flydubai flight traveling from Dubai to Tel Aviv in Israel. The Omani co-pilot stabbed the captain and caused the aircraft to plunge roughly 17,400 feet in under two minutes yesterday.However, passengers and crew members, including off-duty personnel, breached the cockpit, subdued the attacker, and helped stabilise the plane. The flight was diverted and landed safely at Tabuk Regional Airport in northwestern Saudi Arabia.Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defence Minister Israel Katz described the event as a severe security incident and a suspected terrorist attack.The Israeli Prime Minister described Captain Smit Machchhar, an Indian national, as a true hero who saved the lives of 174 people on board the Israel-bound flight. Mr Netanyahu said Captain Smit Machchhar displayed extraordinary bravery by fighting back and preventing a mid-air disaster.US President Donald Trump also hailed Captain Smit Machchhar as a hero for fighting off a knife attack from the Omani co-pilot, opening the cockpit door and calling for help to foil a bid to crash the aircraft.India’s Embassy in Riyadh and its Consulate General in Jeddah said they are closely monitoring the health of Captain Smit Machchhar. In a statement, the Indian Embassy said Captain Machchhar is currently admitted to a hospital in Tabuk and receiving medical treatment.The embassy said initial reports indicate that his condition is stable. The Indian mission said it is in touch with Captain Machchhar’s family and is extending all possible assistance in coordination with the Saudi authorities.

. At least nine Afghan civilians, including women and children, were killed and 11 others injured in Pakistani airstrikes on civilian homes in Afghanistan’s Kunar and Helmand provinces, according to Taliban spokesperson Zabihullah Mujahid. He said the strikes yesterday also destroyed three residences in the Shultan district of Kunar and Garmser district of Helmand.The latest attacks come amid an escalation in Pakistani airstrikes across several Afghan provinces. Mujahid said four civilians were killed in strikes in Kandahar, Paktia and Khost on September 24, while three people were killed in attacks in Kunar and Paktika three days earlier.Condemning the latest strikes as an act of aggression, Mujahid accused Pakistan of using attacks on Afghanistan to divert attention from domestic political and economic problems. He also warned that Afghanistan would give an “appropriate response” to what he described as Pakistani military aggression.

. Poland has called for stronger and more stable economic and trade ties with India, with Polish Finance and Economy Minister Andrzej Domański describing India as a global economic leader and an important partner.Domański said Poland sees India as a major, fast-growing economy and a democracy with which it wants to build long-term commercial relations, reports said.Speaking on the sidelines of the G20 Trade Ministers’ Meeting in Milwaukee, the Polish minister said Warsaw wants Poland, the European Union and India to become much closer trade partners.He stressed that greater predictability in economic relations is increasingly important in a rapidly changing global environment, adding that India-Poland trade relations still have significant potential for further expansion.India and Poland upgraded their ties to a Strategic Partnership during Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s visit to Warsaw in August 2024.An action plan for 2024 to 2028 covers trade and investment, defence and security, technology, energy and other areas, while India and the European Union are also pursuing deeper trade and investment cooperation.

. A flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv made an emergency landing at Tabuk Airport in Saudi Arabia today after an incident on board that reportedly involved one of the pilots being stabbed. Flight FZ1073, carrying around 180 passengers, including several Israeli nationals, was en route from Dubai to Tel Aviv when the incident occurred.According to passenger accounts reported by Israeli media, passengers helped crew members restrain an attacker. An emergency signal, or squawk code 7700, was initially transmitted by the aircraft, followed briefly by code 7500, which indicates hijacking or unlawful interference. Media reports said, the Boeing 737 MAX made a sharp descent during the flight, dropping from around 34 thousand feet to approximately 17 thousand feet in less than a minute. Reports also indicate one pilot attempted to crash the aircraft.Israeli Air Force fighter jets were reportedly scrambled to intercept the aircraft after Israeli authorities were unable to establish contact with it. The aircraft later re-established contact and landed safely at Tabuk Airport.The Israeli Prime Minister’s Office said Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu held consultations following concerns over the aviation incident and was monitoring developments. It said the incident was under control and that measures were being taken to return the Israeli passengers safely to Israel.Flydubai confirmed that Flight FZ1073 had experienced an incident while en route from Dubai to Tel Aviv. However, the exact circumstances surrounding the incident have not yet been confirmed by flydubai. The airline said the aircraft landed safely in Tabuk and that all passengers and crew were safe and accounted for.Flydubai said it was working closely with the relevant authorities and was also sending another aircraft to Tabuk to transport the stranded passengers to Tel Aviv. The incident remains under investigation.

. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh has said that the same spirit of synergy and integration currently being emphasised among the three armed forces needs to be implemented within the financial framework of the Defence Accounts Department as well.Addressing the Defence Accounts Day in New Delhi today, he said that if the financial systems are also integrated, the entire defence management will become even more efficient. He said that this department serves as a common thread connecting the entire Ministry of Defence and is the backbone of the defence system.The Minister urged them to adopt and internalise the best practices in quality auditing at both the national and international levels and keep pace with evolving standards across the country and the world. Mr Singh stated that, during the last financial year, expenditure booking stood at approximately 100 percent.He said, this achievement marks a significant milestone and is a testament to the concerted efforts of the Defence Accounts Department and the three Services.The Minister added that this achievement reflects their unwavering commitment, dedication, hard work, and efficiency in ensuring the effective utilisation of resources.During the event, the Defence Minister launched several Information Technology initiatives of the Defence Accounts Department aimed at strengthening financial management and digital systems within the Ministry of Defence.These include the integration of the Indian Army Financial Information System with the Department’s SAKSHAM platform, the revamped National Compilation System for the Ministry of Defence, and the Payment Routing and Integrated System Management (PRISM) platform.

. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu today said, that Saudi authorities have arrested the pilot of a Flydubai flight who allegedly stabbed another pilot and attempted to crash the aircraft carrying Israeli passengers. Mr. Netanyahu said passengers and crew members managed to subdue the attacker, preventing what he described as a major disaster. He praised those on board for their courage and quick response, saying they had saved many lives.The incident occurred on a commercial flight travelling from the United Arab Emirates to Israel. A reported altercation between the pilots forced the aircraft to make an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia.According to Israeli media reports, an Indian national was the captain of Flydubai flight FZ1073 while the co-pilot was an Omani national who was suspected of attempting to crash the aircraft. The report said the Indian captain fought with the co-pilot to prevent the aircraft from crashing. Reports said, the signal was apparently triggered by an altercation between the pilots in the cockpit. Israeli passengers later intervened and helped restrain the co-pilot. The aircraft subsequently landed safely at Tabuk airport in Saudi Arabia.Israeli government said the situation was under control and efforts were underway to bring the passengers home.Meanwhile, the Israel Airports Authority has opened a dedicated waiting and information area at Ben Gurion Airport for the families of passengers aboard a Tel Aviv-bound flydubai flight that was diverted to Saudi Arabia.

. In Men’s Cricket, the second ODI of the three-match series between India and West Indies will be played at Barsapara Cricket Stadium in Guwahati today. The match will begin at 2:00 PM.After a convincing eight-wicket victory in the opening match in Thiruvananthapuram, India aims to extend their lead in the series and establish an insurmountable advantage. With Virat Kohli and Shubman Gill each scoring a century in the first ODI, the hosts are confident going into the second game and looking to continue their strong batting performance.The West Indies, on the other hand, are eager to bounce back after their heavy defeat in the opening match. The visitors will need to improve both their batting and pitching and find a way to contain India’s experienced batsmen. With the series still open, the West Indies are hoping for a significantly improved performance in Guwahati to level the series score.

. The Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA) facilitated the flag-off of a one MT consignment of GI-tagged Gulbarga Tur Dal from Karnataka to the Maldives. The consignment, exported yesterday by M/s Silken Global Exports and Imports, Mysuru, through its Farmer Producer Organisation (FPO)-led brand, will be transported to the Maldives by sea. The Ministry of Commerce and Industry said that the initiative is aimed at expanding international markets for India’s GI-tagged agricultural products and strengthening the participation of FPO-led brands in agri exports.It added that a key feature of the export-linked value chain is improved price realisation for farmers, which enables farmers to realise 82 rupees per kg against prevailing market price of 60 rupees per kg. It provides FPOs an opportunity to participate more closely in export-oriented value chains and connect producers with international markets. The Ministry further noted that the export is expected to pave the way for regular shipments of Gulbarga Tur Dal to the Maldives, creating sustained market opportunities for producers and exporters from Karnataka. The initiative is also expected to support greater value realisation for farmers and enable FPOs and farmers to integrate more closely with export-oriented value chains.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi said that the country is moving rapidly on the Reform Express and the institutions that conduct examinations must also work on reforms that are the need of the country.Addressing the Centenary Celebrations of the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi today, Mr Modi said that an examination should not be considered just an event as it is related to the future of the youth.Mr Modi noted that a delay of even a few months can create difficulties for the youth, and therefore, the examination system should follow the principle of time certainty.Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said that over the 100-year journey of UPSC, the generations, governments, technology, and syllabi have changed, but the trust in this institution remains as unwavering as ever.Mr Modi stressed the need to bring young people into public services who are drawn not to public office but to public service. He said, today, 21st-century India is moving forward with a new work culture and its core principle is Pro-People, Pro-Active, Good Governance.The Prime Minister said his Government’s mantra is Nagarik Devo Bhava and serving the citizens is paramount. He said, for a Viksit Bharat, the kind of governance the country now needs will be enabled to a great extent by institutions such as the UPSC and the State Public Service Commissions. Mr Modi said the young people being recruited today will play an important role in building a Viksit Bharat.Prime Minister Modi said India in 2047 will be very different from the India of today. He said India will be more urban, the gap between villages and cities will be smaller, and the aspirations and expectations of the citizens, especially the youth, will be much higher. He said the next 20 to 25 years will be extremely important for every Indian and for every institution in the country.Minister of State for Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions Dr Jitendra Singh said that UPSC has achieved several milestones and added many new dimensions during the last twelve years.He said the number of government appointments made through UPSC has increased, and transparency in the recruitment system has also improved, leading to greater public trust.Dr Singh highlighted that approximately 65 thousand appointments were made through the UPSC during the NDA’s 12-year tenure, compared with around 45 thousand appointments during the UPA’s ten-year tenure. The Minister said that today, UPSC has become a role model for recruitment agencies across the country and the world.Chairman UPSC Dr Ajay Kumar said, since independence, generations of the nation’s youth have come to the Commission’s doorstep with dreams of serving the country and UPSC has ensured that they are judged solely on the touchstone of merit. He said, currently, women constitute approximately 30 per cent of the successful candidates in the Civil Services Examination.Dr Kumar said, measures such as identifying duplicate applications with the help of Artificial Intelligence, real-time OCR-based evaluation of millions of documents uploaded by candidates and face authentication for lakhs of candidates at examination centers are some of the recent steps adopted by the Commission to further strengthen fairness and security.The programme marks the culmination of year-long celebrations that commenced on 1st October last year, commemorating 100 years since the establishment of the UPSC in 1926.On the occasion, Prime Minister Modi released a UPSC Centenary Commemorative Coin, a Commemorative Stamp and a Book titled ‘100 Landmark Judgements – Shaping the Policies of UPSC and Public Service Commissions in India ‘.

. The ninth Deputy National Security Adviser-level meeting of the Colombo Security Conclave, CSC, was hosted virtually by India today. The meeting was attended by representatives from Bangladesh, Maldives, Mauritius, Sri Lanka and Seychelles.The Ministry of External Affairs said the member states reviewed the decisions taken at the seventh National Security Adviser-level meeting of the CSC, held in New Delhi on 20th November last year. They also reviewed the Roadmap for Cooperation and Activities for 2025-26 and noted substantial progress made by member states in organising training and capacity-building programmes across the five pillars of cooperation. The Ministry said the member states reiterated their resolve to further strengthen cooperation on key security issues in the Indian Ocean Region and continue their enduring partnership in humanitarian assistance and disaster relief. Deputy National Security Adviser for Strategic Affairs Pavan Kapoor led the Indian delegation.

. In Men’s cricket, India crushed the West Indies by eight wickets in the second ODI of the three-match series at Barsapara Cricket Stadium in Guwahati last night, taking an unassailable 2-nil lead.Put into bat, West Indies posted their highest-ever ODI total of 405 for seven, powered by centuries from John Campbell, Shai Hope and Amir Jangoo.In reply, India comfortably chased down the target in 43.3 overs, losing only two wickets. Captain Shubman Gill led the charge with a sensational unbeaten 233 off 133 balls, while Rohit Sharma scored 101 off 75 balls to register his 35th ODI century.The Indian opening pair put on a record-breaking 255-run partnership for the first wicket. Gill also became the fastest player to score a double century in ODI cricket, reaching the landmark in just 117 balls, while his unbeaten 233 became the highest individual score by an Indian in an ODI run chase. Gill was named Player of the Match for his outstanding innings.India had also won the opening ODI in Thiruvananthapuram by eight wickets. The third and final match of the series will be played on Saturday in New Chandigarh.

. The All India Consumer Products Federation and the All India Mobile Retailers Association have decided to withdraw their proposed call for a ‘No UPI Day’ on Friday.The decision was taken following a meeting between a delegation of around 20 senior trade leaders, led by BJP MP and Secretary General of the Confederation of All India Traders, Praveen Khandelwal, and Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman in New Delhi. During the meeting, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman assured the delegation that the government remains committed to promoting digital transactions while safeguarding the interests of all stakeholders.The trade leaders reiterated their full support for the Digital India mission and the success of UPI, which has emerged as a global model for digital payments. The delegation expressed confidence that continued dialogue between the government and trade bodies would help evolve a practical and sustainable framework to further strengthen India’s digital economy.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi today congratulated Neeru Dhanda and Kynan Chenai on bringing home the Gold medal in the Trap Mixed Team event at the 2026 Asian Games.In a social media post, Mr Modi said that the Indian pair created an Asian Record in the Final to secure India’s first-ever Asian Games Gold in this event. Lauding their performance, he said that it is a memorable achievement for Indian shooting.The Prime Minister also congratulated Jyothi Surekha Vennam, Prithika Pradeep and Chikitha Taniparthi on winning the Gold Medal in the Women’s Compound Team event at the Asian Games 2026. Mr Modi said that this is even more special because their performance also equalled the World Record. Hailing their performance, the Prime Minister said that this is a tremendous achievement for the Indian archers. Mr Modi extended his wishes to the athletes for their future endeavours.

. The Ministry of Mines will launch the auction of offshore mineral blocks today. The Ministry said that this marks an important step towards unlocking India’s offshore mineral potential and strengthening the country’s long-term mineral resource security.The auction comprises two offshore mineral blocks in the Andaman Sea region, which will be offered for grant of a composite licence.The Ministry underlined that it is expected to encourage systematic exploration, attract investment and promote the adoption of advanced technologies for offshore mineral exploration and development.The Ministry also said that offshore mineral resources are important in the context of technological advancement, clean energy transition and resilient supply chains.

. Brazil and India are moving to significantly expand their existing preferential trade agreement with Mercosur, the South American trade bloc that includes Brazil and other South American economies.Brazilian Development, Industry, Trade and Services Minister Márcio Elias Rosa said the current pact covers only around 450 tariff lines and is too limited.Speaking after a meeting with India’s Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal on the sidelines of the G20 Trade Ministers’ Meeting in Milwaukee, Rosa said both sides have completed the terms of reference for broader negotiations. He said the framework would enable the two sides to begin building concrete proposals for an expanded trade agreement.The discussions are also looking at deeper cooperation in areas including the bioeconomy, circular economy and digital economy, along with artificial intelligence, skills development and defence. The move could broaden trade and economic ties between India and Mercosur.

. The Government has reduced the stock holding period for sugar dealers to 15 days and fixed the stock holding limit at one thousand quintals, with effect from the 15th of this month. It will remain effective till November this year.Consumer Affairs Ministry said that the government has revised the sugar stock holding norms to prevent hoarding and ensure smooth supply to consumers during the festive season.Under the revised provisions, the stock holding limit for Kolkata and its extended metropolitan areas and Assam have been fixed at two thousand quintals.The Ministry said, Kolkata sources sugar from Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra and Karnataka and supplies it to the eastern part of the country, including the North-Eastern region.The higher limit for Assam has been provided keeping in view geographical constraints, transportation logistics and consumer interest in the North-Eastern region.The Ministry said that average retail sugar prices have declined by 15 per cent from their August peak and are expected to decline further. Ex-mill sugar prices have also declined by approximately 28 per cent and have remained stable over the last three weeks.The decline reflects the impact of various measures taken by the Government to ensure adequate availability of sugar and facilitate its orderly movement through the market. Wholesalers and retailers have also been urged to immediately pass on the benefit of the substantial decline in ex-mill sugar prices to consumers.

. India has cautioned against treating legitimate national measures to protect food security as the weaponisation of food. Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal made the distinction during a session of the G20 Trade Ministers’ Meeting in Milwaukee, US. Goyal highlighted that the shared objective must be to ensure that food remains a source of security, stability and cooperation.The Minister also reviewed progress towards the signing and entry into force of the India-European Union Free Trade Agreement. He held talks with European Commissioner for Trade and Economic Security Maroš Šefčovič on the sidelines of the G20 Trade Ministers’ Meeting.The two sides also exchanged views on the India-EU Trade and Technology Council, reform of the World Trade Organisation and shared priorities at the G20.India and the EU concluded negotiations for the trade pact on January 27 this year, after talks that began in 2007 and were relaunched in 2022.The European Commission earlier this month submitted the agreement to the EU Council for authorisation for signature and conclusion.Minister of State for Commerce and Industry Jitin Prasada has said the pact would create greater opportunities for trade and investment, while technology transfers, local manufacturing and artificial intelligence would support India’s next phase of industrial growth.

. The Bangladesh Government is committed to ensuring a safe, peaceful and festive environment for the celebration of Durga Puja 2026 across the country, Religious Affairs Minister Mohammad Shamim Kaiser has said.The Minister made the remarks at an inter-ministerial preparatory meeting to review arrangements for Durga Puja 2026 yesterday. Security has also been stepped up across the country to ensure that the upcoming Durga Puja is celebrated in a peaceful, festive and secure atmosphere.The State Minister said the government is committed to ensuring the safe and festive celebration of Durga Puja, described as the main religious festival of the country’s Hindu community. He directed relevant authorities to ensure the smooth distribution of grants from the Puja Welfare Trust to puja committees across the country.He also stressed enhanced vigilance by local administrations and law enforcement agencies in view of the increase in the number of puja mandaps. The State Minister called for maintaining social and religious harmony and urged people to respect traditional practices, including maintaining silence during the Azan and prayers.He directed intelligence and law enforcement agencies to take immediate legal action against those spreading rumours through old or edited content on social media and called for impartial investigations into any untoward incidents. Representatives of various ministries, security agencies and Hindu, Buddhist and Christian organisations attended the meeting.

. India enjoyed its most successful day at the ongoing Asian Games in Japan so far, winning four gold medals today. The country completed a hat-trick of gold medals in compound archery, with the women’s team, mixed team and men’s team all finishing on top. India also struck gold in shooting, with the mixed trap team securing the top spot. Indian boxers added two more bronze medals to the tally, with Priya Ghanghas and Kapil Pokhariya finishing on the podium today. Boxer Narendra Berwal had bagged the bronze yesterday.Later in the day, Wrestler Sunil Kumar won bronze in the men’s 87kg Greco-Roman event, beating the Philippines’ Callum Johnston Roberts 9-nil. Kumar, who also won bronze at Hangzhou 2022, became the first Indian wrestler to win multiple Greco-Roman medals at the Asian Games.In Women’s Hockey, India defeated South Korea 2-nil this evening to reach the final. Ishika Chaudhary and Captain Salima Tete scored for India. India will face defending champions China in final on Friday. India are now just a victory away from securing its only second Asian Games women’s hockey gold medal, with their only previous triumph coming way back in 1982.In Squash, India’s Men’s and Women’s teams advanced to the semifinals, assuring two more medals. The top-seeded and defending champion Men’s team beat Kuwait 2-Nil, while the Women’s team defeated Singapore by the same margin. India have already won two Singles silver medals in Squash through Abhay Singh and Anahat Singh, and a mixed doubles bronze through Joshna Chinappa and Velavan Senthilkumar.With these victories, India’s medal tally has risen to 60, including 10 gold, 21 silver and 29 bronze medals.

. US President Donald Trump announced that the final contingent of American troops is leaving Iraq, formally concluding Operation Inherent Resolve.Addressing the media, Trump described the withdrawal as a decisive victory over ISIS and said it represented a victory for the United States as well as a victory for Iraq. He said the withdrawal brings an end to more than two decades of American military involvement in Iraq.The withdrawal plan was negotiated between the United States and Iraq under the Biden administration in 2024, with September 30 set as the final deadline.The Trump administration continued to implement the agreement. US troops first left Iraq in 2011 after an eight-year presence that began with the 2003 US invasion.They returned in 2014 after ISIS seized large parts of Iraq and Syria and threatened the approaches to Baghdad. Although the US-led campaign defeated ISIS militarily in 2019, American forces remained in Iraq to help prevent a resurgence of the group.

. The Supreme Court will tomorrow hear a plea challenging the Centre’s decision to impose a Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on specified UPI person-to-merchant transactions of over 2,000 rupees.Ending nearly six years of fully free UPI payments, the government has introduced a 0.4 per cent fee on transfers of over 2,000 Rs made to merchants through the UPI platform from October 15, while explicitly ring-fencing everyday person-to-person transactions and small payments from any charge. The MDR will be capped at 300 Rs for payments of 75,000 Rs and above.Essential and thin-margin sectors — railways, telecom, insurance, fuel and agricultural inputs — will pay a flat MDR of 5 Rs per transaction above 2,000 Rs.Payments into mutual funds, securities and through stockbrokers and dealers will attract 0.02 per cent MDR, also capped at 300 Rs. Bench of Chief Justice of India Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana will hear the plea.The Public Interest Litigation (PIL) filed by advocate Anjan Datta has challenged the Centre’s decision. The plea alleged that the levy has been introduced without adequate statutory safeguards, transparency or public consultation.

. India’s registered manufacturing sector recorded strong growth in financial year 2025 (FY25), with industrial output rising 7.81 per cent and total employment increasing almost 7.2 per cent over the previous year.According to the Annual Survey of Industries data released by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation today, the total number of establishments in this sector increased from 2.60 lakh in FY24 to 2.67 lakh in FY25, representing a growth of 2.64 per cent. The highest number of establishments was reported in Tamil Nadu, followed by Gujarat and Maharashtra.Meanwhile, total emoluments paid to the workforce also increased by over 12 per cent in 2024-25 on an annual basis. Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, and Haryana have emerged as the top 5 states in employment, having a share of more than 56 per cent of the total manufacturing employment of the country in FY25.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said that safeguarding forests and wildlife is essential for maintaining nature’s balance and securing a valuable legacy for future generations. In his message on the occasion of Wildlife Week 2026, Mr Modi urged citizens to contribute towards protecting wildlife and their habitats.The Prime Minister emphasised that connected habitats and wildlife corridors are essential for the safe movement of animals and maintaining ecological balance. He said that the central government, in collaboration with the states, is continuously working to identify and conserve wildlife corridors.Prime Minister Modi highlighted India’s achievements in wildlife conservation over the past decade, citing the success of Project Cheetah.He also mentioned conservation efforts for species such as the Great Indian Bustard, rhinoceros, river dolphin and snow leopard. Mr Modi also highlighted India’s role in promoting global cooperation for big cat conservation through the International Big Cat Alliance.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices ended on a positive note today. The Sensex rose 315 points to close at 73,896. The Nifty gained 77 points to settle at 23,141. The broader market at the National Stock Exchangedisplayed mixedtrend. The Midcap 100 index dropped over 0.1 per cent, while the Smallcap 100 index rose more than 0.1 per cent.In the forex market, the rupee appreciated by 14 paise to trade at 95 rupees and 82 paise against the US dollar.In the global crude oil market, Brent Crude was trading one per cent down at 105 US dollars and five cents per barrel, while WTI Crude was trading 1.7 per cent lower at 92 US dollars and 99 cents per barrel in intra-day trade.At the Multi Commodity Exchange, Gold for the October contract was trading 0.7 per cent up at 1,51,709 rupees per 10 grams, and Silver for the December contract was trading 1.3 per cent higher at 2,36,574 rupees per kilogram, when reports last came in.For more updates about the market activities, tune in to Akashvani’s bilingual programme ‘Market Mantra’ at 6:30 PM this evening.

Indian athletes will be in action across several disciplines at the Asian Games today.  In Archery, India’s men’s compound team will face South Korea in the semifinal at 10:55 a.m., followed by the medal matches, subject to qualification.In Boxing, Lovlina Borgohain will compete in the women’s 75-kilogram semifinal at 10:45 a.m., while Kapil Pokhariya will contest the men’s 90-kilogram semifinal at noon. North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO) Secretary-General Mark Rutte today accused Russia of carrying out a campaign of hostile actions against NATO allies and said that Moscow was failing to stop the 32-member military alliance’s support for Ukraine. While addressing a joint press conference with Lithuanian Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevicius, Rutte reiterated NATO’s support for Ukraine and said that Russia is failing on the battlefield in Ukraine and in undermining the military alliance’s support for Kyiv.

In Ladakh, RNU Akashvani Kargil has launched a special podcast series under the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan, with the first programme focusing on “Natural Farming – Towards Sustainable and Climate-Resilient Agriculture.”The programme featured Dr. Nazir Hussain, Scientist, Krishi Vigyan Kendra Kargil, in conversation with Anayat Ali of RNU Akashvani Kargil.During the podcast, Dr. Nazir Hussain explained the principles of natural farming and highlighted its role in improving soil health, reducing dependence on external chemical inputs and promoting sustainable and climate-resilient agriculture.He discussed various aspects of the National Mission on Natural Farming, including chemical-free cultivation, livestock integration, diversified cropping, use of locally available bio-inputs and integration of traditional agricultural knowledge with scientific practices.Dr. Hussain said natural farming has considerable potential in Ladakh and Kargil, where agriculture is characterised by a short growing season, cold climatic conditions and limited water availability. He stressed the need for locally adapted practices, scientific research, farmer training and awareness for its successful adoption in the region.Comparing natural farming with organic farming, Dr. Hussain said natural farming can be more effective and efficient in boosting production while reducing farmers’ dependence on externally purchased inputs.The discussion also covered crop productivity, input costs, farmers’ income, water management, climate resilience and the need to make the transition towards natural farming economically viable for farmers.The special podcast series, produced by RNU Akashvani Kargil under the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan, will be broadcast daily at 4:30 PM from Akashvani Kargil. The programmes will also be available on the AIRNews Kargil YouTube channel.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices declined sharply by over 1.5% today. The Sensex plunged 1,240 points to close at 72,772. The Nifty shed 360 points to settle at 22 thousand 780. In the broader market at the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index tumbled 1.6%, while the Smallcap 100 index tanked 1.8%.In the Sensex pack, 29 of the 30 constituent companies logged losses, with Infosys emerging as the lone gainer, rising 0.2%. Among the top underperformers, Larsen and Toubro slumped 2.8%, PowerGrid declined 2.6%, and Adani Ports fell 2.4%.In the sectoral indices on the BSE, all 28 sectors edged lower. Among the top laggards,PSU Banks skidded 3.2%, Power, Telecommunication, and Utilities lost 2.3% each and Mid-Small Private Banks dropped 2.2%.The overall market breadth at the BSE was negative, as shares of 3218 companies declined, 1271 advanced and 228 remained unchanged.

. Chief Economic Adviser V. Anantha Nageswaran has highlighted India’s ability to attract foreign capital with its broader manufacturing and overall reforms. Addressing the 13th PAFI annual forum in New Delhi, Mr Nageswaran emphasized that the most important thing for the industry is global competitiveness. He added that the global environment in which investment decisions are made has now shifted, making it important to assess India’s foreign direct investment performance in that context.Mr Nageswaran also pointed to investor protection, tax-policy certainty and consistency, and availability of skilled talent and logistics as other factors that can influence investment decisions. He noted that changing global interest-rate environments could also have a significant bearing on the cost of capital and cross-border investment flows.

. Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) have offloaded Indian equities worth 17,131 crore rupees in September so far. According to the latest depository data, out of the total net outflows, 25,682 crore rupees were withdrawn through sales on stock exchanges, as geopolitical uncertainty, elevated US bond yields, and crude oil prices weighed on investors’ risk appetite. However, the trend of FPI investment through the primary market has continued this month, with FPIs infusing 8,551 crore rupees in the primary market in September so far.Meanwhile, Foreign investors also extended their selling to the debt market during the period under review. In September so far, outflows from the debt securities through the Fully Accessible Route (FAR) stood at 7,385 crore rupees. FPIs have withdrawn 3,021 crore rupees through the Voluntary Retention Route (VRR) and 1,889 crore rupees through the General Limit route.

. The nationwide Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath cleanliness drive is being conducted as part of the Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 Campaign. The objective of the campaign is to ensure cleanliness, improve sanitation and create awareness about hygiene and proper waste disposal among the general public.Several Union Ministers, the Chief Minister and senior officials are participating in the cleanliness drive across the country. The Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 Campaign, which began on 17th of last month, will be observed till the 17th of October.The theme of this year’s campaign is – Swachhata Mein Sahbhag, Swachh Bharat, and Viksit Bharat, which underlines the role of collective participation and shared responsibility in advancing the vision of a Swachh and Viksit Bharat.Union Jal Shakti Minister C R Paatil participated in a Shramdaan activity at Kalindi Kunj Ghat in New Delhi. Talking to reporters, Mr Paatil said that cleanliness and water conservation are inseparable and emphasised the need to keep rivers clean. He said that treating rivers as garbage bins and dumping waste into them will pollute the water and adversely affect human life.Law and Justice Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal participated in the campaign at Safdarjung Tomb in the national capital. Addressing the gathering, Mr Meghwal said that cleanliness should not be limited to a one-day campaign but should become a daily responsibility. He said that cleanliness has improved significantly across India since 2014, including at railway stations and public places.Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju attended the Swachhata Hi Seva programme at Peshwa Road Navyug School in the national capital. He said Prime Minister Narendra Modi has placed special emphasis on cleanliness and sanitation.Mr Rijiju said that a cleaner India will lead to a healthier India. Union Minister for Coal and Mines G Kishan Reddy also participated in the cleanliness drive in Delhi. Speaking on the occasion, Mr Reddy said, ‘Cleanliness is not just about cleaning, but it should be a part of the behaviour.Union Education Minister Pralhad Joshi also undertook the Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 cleanliness drive at Gargi College in New Delhi. During the drive, he interacted with the students, including those from the NSS, NCC and sports communities and appreciated their enthusiasm and active participation. Mr Joshi said that the students’ commitment to cleanliness and civic responsibility was truly encouraging.

Bangladesh has announced a five-day break for the upcoming Sharadiya Durga Puja, with the official festival holiday extended to three days.Making the announcement, Bangladesh Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed today said, combined with the regular Friday and Saturday weekend, the decision will provide a total five-day holiday. The Home Minister made the announcement following a high-level coordination meeting on security arrangements for the peaceful celebration of Durga Puja. He said the decision to extend the holiday was taken in response to longstanding demands from the Hindu community.The Bangladesh government has also increased the allocation for Durga Puja mandaps to five crore taka from four crore taka, following directives from Prime Minister Tarique Rahman. The Home Minister said, the number of puja mandaps across Bangladesh has risen by nearly 1,500 from last year to 33,851. He added that government agencies at the national, divisional, district and upazila levels have been assigned responsibility for ensuring security and the smooth conduct of the celebrations.Twenty-four-hour monitoring cells will also operate at Police Headquarters and at the divisional and district police levels throughout the festival.

. India’s Women’s Squash team reached the Asian Games semifinals with a 2-0 win over Singapore today, assuring a medal for the country. Tanvi Khanna beat Au Yeong Wai Iynn 11-6, 4-11, 15-13, 11-1 before Anahat Singh defeated Au Yeong Wai Yhann 11-7, 11-3, 11-4. Veteran Joshna Chinappa did not need to play. India will face its Semifinal opponent at Nagoya Kinjo Futo Arena tomorrow. India had topped Pool C after wins over China, Japan and Iran.In Men’s Greco-Roman Wrestling, Sunil Kumar advanced to the Semifinals of 87 kg category today after defeating Tajikistan’s Muhammad Sultonzoda 9-0 by technical superiority in the first period. The 2023 Hangzhou bronze medalist dominated the bout and sealed victory with consecutive gut-wrench moves after Sultonzoda was placed in the par terre position. Sunil is likely to face Japan’s Taizo Yoshida in the Semifinals. However, in the Women’s 68 kg round of 16, Nisha Dahiya lost to North Korea’s Pak Sol Gum.

The government has clarified that a Gazette notification circulating on social media claiming that all Saturdays have been declared public holidays for public sector banks is fake.In a social media post, the Fact Check Unit of the Press Information Bureau said that no such notification has been issued by the Union Finance Ministry. The Ministry of Education, in coordination with the External Affairs Ministry is organizing a two day Bharat Innovates Exposition from today at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi to showcase India’s Deep-Tech innovations as a lead up to and alongside the 18th BRICS Summit 2026. The Exposition is showcasing 37 India’s Deep-Tech startups and ventures alligning with the theme of India’s BRICS Chairship Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability. The event is providing participating innovators an opportunity to network with CEOs, investors, business leaders and industry representatives from BRICS member countries. Ministry of Eduaction said that the event will facilitate opportunities for Business to Business engagements, technology partnerships, investment discussions, business linkages and international market access.

. Science and Technology Minister Dr Jitendra Singh has said that critical minerals are key to India’s energy security, industrial competitiveness and national security. The Minister said this while addressing a special plenary of the 3rd Global Summit on Advanced Materials, Critical Minerals, and Metals in New Delhi. Dr Singh said that critical minerals and metals will be a driving component of the next phase of technological development, with their importance extending beyond mining to energy security, industrial competitiveness and national security. He said that the global economy is undergoing a paradigm shift, with clean energy, electric mobility, semiconductors, telecommunications, aerospace, defence and nuclear energy emerging as major drivers of technological and industrial transformation. He added, India is now participating in this global discourse with much greater confidence and is preparing to assume a larger global role.Dr. Singh has called for early industry linkage with research and innovation, saying potential industry partners should be brought on board right from the beginning. He further said that a healthy synergy among research, industry, government and the non-government sector is essential for sustaining startups and entrepreneurs. The Minister also highlighted on building domestic capabilities for energy security as the world moves towards cleaner and greener sources of energy. He said that India’s next phase of growth in strategic technologies and materials will depend on working together of all stakeholders.

. At the Asian Games 2026, India’s compound mixed archery team of Sahil Jadhav and Chikitha Taniparthi has won a gold medal, beating Korea in a shoot-off in the finals. The Indian duo also secured a 2028 Olympic quota place with this win. They defeated Thailand in the Semi-finals.Earlier, the Indian Women’s Compound Archery team clinched gold after beating China 238-234 in the finals today at Okazaki Chuo Sogo Park, Japan. The Indian team, comprising Jyothi Surekha Vennam, Chikitha Taniparthi and Prithika Pradeep, entered the finals after beating South Korea 234-233 in the semifinals. India won gold in the Women’s compound team event at the 2023 Asian Games in Hangzhou. India now has a total of 54 medals, including eight gold, 21 silver and 25 bronze medals.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is completing 25 years in public service, a journey defined by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues. Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives. Today, in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated into creation of the post of Chief of Defence Staff.Earlier, India’s three armed services – Army, Navy and the Air Force – planned, trained, procured and advised the government separately. Proposals for greater jointness had been made repeatedly since the Kargil Review Committee of 1999 and the Group of Ministers that followed it, but no single officer held authority across all three services. On the 15th of August 2019, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, in his Independence Day address, announced the creation of the post of Chief of Defence Staff from the ramparts of the Red Fort. Prime Minister Modi said this will lead to better coordination among the three services.The Cabinet approved the decision in December 2019, along with a new Department of Military Affairs within the Ministry of Defence for the CDS to head.  Talking to Akashvani News, retired Lt General Sanjay Kulkarni said the appointment of CDS made it possible for the government to have one point of contact for advice on allmiltarymatters.After the formation of the post of CDS, all three forces have now got effective leadership at the top level.

. Today is World Suicide Prevention Day. The day is observed worldwide to raise awareness about suicide prevention and the importance of mental health.The occasion reminds us that people facing emotional distress or difficult circumstances need timely support, understanding and appropriate care. Experts emphasise that listening to someone with patience and without judgement can encourage them to seek help and support.On this Day, people are encouraged to remain attentive to the emotional well-being of those around them and, when required, guide them towards family members, trusted persons or mental health professionals.

. The Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Act has come into force today. The Act has amended the Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969. The objective of this act is to prevent delays in the registration of births and deaths and to encourage people to register in a timely manner.The act provides that if a birth or death is reported to the Registrar more than one year but within two years, it may be registered only with the approval of the District Magistrate, Sub-Divisional Magistrate, or an Executive Magistrate.According to the act, a birth or death that is reported to the Registrar for more than two years will only be registered upon a Judicial Magistrate of the First Class’s order.The Act also mandates that the designated authority must verify the authenticity of the reported birth or death before granting permission for delayed registration.The registration of births and deaths is mandatory, and the certificate issued provides legal identity to an individual. The Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Bill was passed by Parliament during the Monsoon Session in August this year.

. Supreme Court has ruled out a complete ban on firecrackers ahead of Diwali and favoured a balanced approach. A bench of Justices MM Sundresh and PB Varale indicated it will permit the use of certain firecrackers during Diwali but impose specified time limits, ruling out both a blanket ban and unrestricted bursting of crackers.The apex court stressed the need to strike a balance between religious sentiments and the harmful effects of air pollution. It said a complete ban could hurt the sentiments of people celebrating Diwali, while allowing firecrackers throughout the day will adversely affect the environment and vulnerable groups, including children, the elderly and the sick.The apex court was hearing a long-pending matter concerning restrictions on firecrackers in Delhi-NCR and other northern states during the period of severe air pollution. The bench also indicated that it is inclined to accept a suggestion to permit joint firecrackers, or ‘larri’, subject to conditions.Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati sought time till October 15 to place on record the Central Pollution Control Board’s report on barium-based firecrackers, saying outdoor testing of such crackers is yet to be conducted. The bench granted the time sought and said it will consider the report before deciding which categories of firecrackers can be permitted.

The second edition of the India Art, Architecture and Design Biennale (IAADB) will be held from 4th December 2026 to 21st March 2027 in New Delhi.The theme of this 108-day Biennale is ‘Tat Tvam Asi – Reconnecting in an Age of Distraction’. Talking exclusively to Akashvani News, Secretary of the Ministry of Culture, Vivek Aggarwal said that, the Biennale will feature art installations at iconic heritage sites of the National Capital, including Purana Qila, Red Fort, Safdarjung Tomb, Qutub Minar, Qila Rai Pithora and Lodhi Garden. He said that the theme of this year’s Biennale directly takes inspiration from India’s ancient traditions and spiritual thought, which emphasize self-introspection and the unity of the individual with the larger universal consciousness.Mr Aggarwal said that the Ministry aims to take IAADB to a global level by encouraging participation from international pavilions and artists, Indian states and the private sector.Speaking about the cultural diplomacy of India, He said that cultural exchange is an important component of cultural diplomacy and the country’s soft power. Mr Aggarwal added that participation of foreign countries will provide an opportunity for Indian and international audiences to experience diverse art forms and will help position the Biennale on the global cultural calendar.Underlining the importance of Art and Design students in this Biennale, He said that the Ministry plans to involve students, particularly those pursuing art and design, in various activities associated with the Biennale, providing them opportunities to engage with artists and the wider creative ecosystem.The second edition of the India Art, Architecture & Design Biennale 2026 is the largest platform which offers artists, curators, galleries, corporates, architects, designers, cultural institutions and other stakeholders a chance to connect with culture and the creative world. This edition is conceived not as a single exhibition in a single location but as a city-wide cultural platform. Visitors will have an opportunity to experience the historical monuments along with contemporary art installations.
